dates.note: The node's exemplar says 1897-1900; the notice prints 'Année(s) de(s) campagne(s) de construction 1900' and 'Construit pour exposition universelle de 1900'. As at the Grand Palais the register records the completion, not the start.

refs.title: Petit Palais, actuellement musée des Beaux-Arts de la Ville de Paris
refs.note: The notice prints 'Nature de la protection de l'édifice inscrit MH' and 'Date et niveau de protection de l'édifice 1975/01/15 : inscrit MH' - INSCRIT, the lower of the two French grades, where its twin across the avenue is CLASSÉ. The reference was read from the fr.wikipedia list of monuments historiques of the 8th arrondissement, which prints 'Petit Palais | Avenue Winston-Churchill | « PA00088878 » | Inscrit | 1975'.

measurements.note: Seven sculptors named in the author field, against two architects. The 'Description historique' field lists EIGHT names, adding 'Hercule' - which is a subject, not a sculptor, and the discrepancy is left as the register prints it. Carried because this node's defining characteristics make concentrated sculpture a defining trait and this is the register counting the hands.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. THE REGISTER GRADES THE TWO 1900 PALACES DIFFERENTLY AND THE CORPUS TREATS THEM ALIKE: the Grand Palais is 'classé' (2000) and the Petit Palais only 'inscrit' (1975), the lower grade. That is a fact about French heritage administration rather than about architecture, and it is recorded because a reader comparing the two records will otherwise wonder. The notice states no material, no dimension and no plan; the trapezoidal site and the semicircular garden court the node values are entirely unsourced here. Hennebique appears in the author field, which is the register's own record of reinforced concrete inside a stone envelope. No rights line was read, so no `rights_evidence`.
